questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to plan production-grade live patching with minimal risk, clear rollback procedures, and end-to-end automation.

## Key Concepts
- Live patching with kpatch or KSP
- Canary and staged rollout strategies
- ABI and module compatibility verification
- Observability: kpatch status, dmesg, perf, IRQ latency
- Automated rollback criteria
- Post-patch validation

## Code Example
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
CANARY_NODES=(host1 host2)
STAGE_PERCENT=20
STAGE_INTERVAL=12
ROLLBACK_LATENCY_PCT=10

for h in "${CANARY_NODES[@]}"; do
  echo "Applying patch to canary: $h"
  ssh "$h" "sudo kpatch load /path/to/patch.kpatch"
  sleep 5
  ssh "$h" "sudo kpatch verify" || { echo "Patch verification failed on $h"; exit 1; }
done

echo "Monitoring canary group for ${STAGE_INTERVAL}h..."
sleep "${STAGE_INTERVAL}h"

for h in "${CANARY_NODES[@]}"; do
  LATENCY=$(ssh "$h" 'perf stat -a sleep 1 2>&1 | grep latency' || echo "0")
  if (( $(echo "$LATENCY > $ROLLBACK_LATENCY_PCT" | bc -l) )); then
    echo "Latency regression detected on $h - rolling back"
    ssh "$h" "sudo kpatch unload /path/to/patch.kpatch"
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "Canary validation passed. Proceeding to staged rollout..."
```

## Why This Question Is Asked
This question assesses practical ability to diagnose and reduce container startup tail latency in multi-tenant Linux environments, requiring a balance between isolation guarantees and throughput performance.

## Key Concepts
- cgroup v2 resource quotas and hierarchy management
- Namespace lifecycle optimization and reuse strategies
- Network namespace (netns) initialization patterns
- Trade-offs between tenant isolation and startup overhead
- Observability tooling: perf, pidstat, BPF, ftrace
- Staged testing methodology and safe rollback procedures

## Architecture Considerations
The solution requires coordinating multiple kernel subsystems (cgroups, namespaces, networking) while maintaining security boundaries. Pre-provisioning shifts setup overhead from container creation time to tenant onboarding, spreading cost over time. Network namespace reuse must be carefully evaluated against tenant isolation requirements—the shared network namespace optimization works best for trust boundaries within the same security domain. Kernel tuning requires balancing latency reduction against fairness and throughput for other tenants on the shared host.

```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/batch.timer
[Timer]
OnCalendar=hourly
Persistent=true
AccuracySec=1s

```
```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/batch.service
[Service]

Group=batch

```
